restrictions: Target sha256-r31-prefix-v1: SHA-256 compression steps 0..30 inclusive on every padded block, standard fixed IV once at the start, FIPS 180-4 padding, full feed-forward, full 256-bit big-endian digest; ordinary collision of two distinct finite byte strings.

The online algorithm is a DETERMINISTIC REPLAY of exactly the two 128-byte messages written out in proof.md Section 3 (first block M0 shared; second blocks M1 and M1' differing only in words W5..W9 by d5..d9). It is not a submitted generator for new collisions.

Algorithmic success_probability is exactly 1: the online algorithm performs no random draws and no search, so there is no trial-count, amplification, chaining-value, matching, or completion-rate term anywhere in the cost argument.

PROVENANCE: the replayed pair's first block M0 and second-block words W0..W12 are the ATTRIBUTED published Li-Liu-Wang matched prefix; only W13,W14,W15 (and hence the five distinct colliding pairs) are our own completion. We did not perform the first-block matching search; the pairs are distinct from the published pair but share its matched prefix. No new or cheaper attack is claimed.

The two-block construction that produced the replayed pair is fully specified in proof.md (characteristic and signed condition table, exact message/expansion differences and constants, the exact admissible sets V5..V8/G16/G18/S with their enumerated sizes, the Phase-1 table equations, the Phase-2 first-block match, and the capped Phase-3 completion). No external paper is relied upon. The characteristic and the matched prefix are the attributed Li-Liu-Wang EUROCRYPT 2024 Sect 4.2 results.

COMPLETE LEDGER: all work that produced the replayed pair is charged once as preprocessing and included in total time, with no cross-target amortization and no parallel wall-time discount. This includes the dominant attributed first-block/practical-attack phase (the published ~2^40.5 target-compressions, whose cost is dominated by the first-block search), our own differential-trail re-derivation (including failed/abandoned branches), the starting-point solve, the table generation, the completion, and all serialization and verification. One target compression costs 1 unit; every other 256-bit word primitive (load, store, add/sub, AND/OR/XOR/NOT, shift/rotate, compare, branch) costs 1/2140 unit. The construction CPU-seconds we measured are converted at 2^24 units per CPU-second; the published first-block phase is charged at its published complexity.

time_log2 is a hard upper bound that holds on every run: the honest construction total is 2^40.914 (attributed first-block 2^40.5 + our trail 2^38.894 + starting-point 2^32.29 + table <=2^30 + completion <=2^18.34), the online replay is <=2^2.67 units (every load, store, compare and the six verification compressions charged), and the sum is <=2^41. There is no probabilistic step.

Memory is a reported metric only, with no scalar contribution and no tie-break; memory_log2_bytes reflects the peak storage of the one-time construction (the SAT solver). baseline_improved = sha256-r31-nominal-v2 is a required reference identifier and does not itself assert an improvement.

Certificates are five distinct colliding pairs with the organizer target profile; the online algorithm replays certificate selfgen-1-replayed. Each shares the attributed published matched prefix but carries our own W13..W15, so each is distinct from the published pair and from the others, and each is re-hashed by the organizer. The stored replayed pair (256 bytes) is the only nonuniform advice the online algorithm consults.

No organizer experiment is requested: a deterministic replay has no empirical or probabilistic premise to test, and H-CONSTRUCTION-COST is a one-time cost bound discharged by the published complexity and our cited measurements, not by a repeated-trial experiment.

heuristics.statement: All one-time work that produced the replayed collision pair is at most 2^40.92 collision-frontier-v5 target-compression units, and the total charged time after the deterministic replay is at most 2^41 units. This construction cost includes the ATTRIBUTED published Li-Liu-Wang first-block/practical-attack phase that produced the matched prefix M0 and W0..W12 (~2^40.5 target-compressions, whose dominant cost is the first-block search), together with our own differential-trail re-derivation (including failed and abandoned branches), the starting-point solve, the table enumeration, the capped completion, and all serialization and verification.
heuristics.scope: The one-time two-block construction specified in proof.md Sections 4-8 that produced the five certificates: the attributed published first-block match (not ours), plus our own trail re-derivation, starting-point solve, table build, and completion of W13..W15. Plus the deterministic online replay of certificate selfgen-1-replayed. Not a per-call or amortized attack cost.
heuristics.extrapolation: The dominant term is the published Li-Liu-Wang 31-step practical-attack complexity ~2^40.5 target-compressions (charged in full, as the two passing replay packages charged it under H-HISTORICAL-TIME), whose cost is dominated by exactly the first-block search that produced M0. This figure is ALREADY in 31-step SHA-256 compressions, which is exactly the collision-frontier-v5 unit, so no publication-to-v5 conversion factor is applied to the dominant term. To it we add our own measured work: trail re-derivation 41 solver calls / 30437.3 CPU-seconds = 2^38.894 units, starting-point generation 313.56 CPU-seconds = 2^32.29 units, table build <= 2^30, and completion per call <= 2^16.02 (five pairs <= 2^18.34); only these own-measured CPU-second terms use the 2^24 units-per-CPU-second calibration. The honest sum is 2^40.914; the online replay adds <= 2^2.67, keeping the total <= 2^41. No allowance factor is needed because the attributed published term already dominates.
heuristics.limitations: The published 2^40.5 figure is the authors' reported practical-attack complexity rather than an organizer-model instruction trace, but it needs no unit conversion (it is already in 31-step compressions = the v5 unit). The 2^24 units-per-CPU-second figure applies only to our own measured trail and starting-point terms, each more than 2 bits below the dominant 2^40.5 term, so the total is insensitive to it: even a 2x calibration error moves the total by under 0.2 bits and it stays under 2^41. Sensitivity: the construction cost enters the total additively and the replay term is negligible; the honest sum 2^40.914 leaves about 6% headroom under 2^41. If a reviewer's accounting pushed the first-block/practical-attack phase materially above 2^40.5, time_log2 must rise to 42; correctness takes priority over the round number.
